name: Mustang Grape

facts.how: Jelly, juice, country wine; raw only in small amounts
facts.where: Fence lines, creek bottoms, woodland edges

caution: Raw juice is harsh with acid and can irritate skin and mouth; wear gloves for big harvests. Confirm the felty white underside of the leaf, since peppervine, which sickens, shares the habit.

sections.title: Harvesting
sections.body: Look for low-hanging clusters on fence lines in high summer, and take only what the vine gives easily. A single healthy mustang vine can carry pounds of fruit, so there is no need to strip any one plant.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: The acid that makes these grapes rough raw is exactly what makes them shine as jelly and wine. Cook, strain, and sweeten, and you get a deep purple preserve that tastes like a Texas summer.
